The Sisyphus is a vessel that would have been out of place in the spacelanes of the Domain era. A tough little ship, visually and even internally, to some extent, reminiscent of a Monitor-class vessel, albeit one capable of carrying not-insignificant amounts of cargo.
Unlike the Monitor, the Sisyphus is not impossibly difficult to destroy, but the additional survivability added by its substantial (for a freighter) armour is not to be understated. In the hauling business, such as it is in the post-Collapse Persean Sector, a few additional seconds can be just enough for a freighter captain to escape from what would have been a loss with all hands and cargo. In fact, the Sisyphus is *designed* around this fact intentionally: its armour and hull are deliberately built so that it can take damage and be returned to service relatively quickly. Just replace the damaged section of armour, seal it back into place and the Sisyphus is ready for shipping once more.

The Praxidike is a unique vessel by pre-Collapse standards, in that it is a dedicated, armoured bulk transport ship, often described as the bastard offspring of an Atlas and a Colossus-class freighter. Indeed, the sheer efficiency of the Atlas appealed to the Strategic Council of the Domain, but its performance in combat conditions left much to be desired. The obvious argument against this was that an Atlas should never see combat in the first place, but after a particularly humiliating incident of elements of a Domain Battlegroup losing their designated supply haulers to rebels, the Praxidike was quietly put into design by Orion Shipyards, the traditional builder of the heavier ships of the Domain Armada such as the notorious Onslaught.

The Goblin Mk.II is an illicit conversion of an already illicit (and infamously mediocre) ship, that being the Goblin, a phase destroyer only slightly more refined than the Gremlin class. The much-hated design has seen a modification by an ambitious and short-lived pirate warlord, the interior completely redesigned to allow the fitting of a drive field stabiliser, more often than not literally ripped from inside an Ox-class tug.

The profoundly disturbing p-space phenomena associated with the Gremlin, and Goblin class have been further amplified by the addition of this stabiliser, which was never intended to be attached to a vessel with a phase coil. Reports of hallucinations, sporadic loss of consciousness and even worse effects abound for those who try to crew a Goblin Mk.II with a clear head. Individual crew members can rarely endure a month aboard a Goblin Mk.II before being rotated out for psychological concerns. A terrible vessel.
Legend says that one of the first Goblin Mk.IIs ever "built" was salvaged from a mercenary convoy that was ambushed by pirates and as such the remains of the original crew were never truly removed, leaving a permanent stench that could not be removed, which was compensated by the crew being given large amounts of mind-altering substances like alcohol, so no different to any other pirate crew.

The Anger is a ship that defies traditional expectations of Domain-era shipbuilding. Originally built out of components intended for a variety of different combat vessel hulls, somehow a cohesive design was created in a hidden shipyard beyond the Core Worlds. Originally the brainchild of a brilliant salvager slash inventor, the design, soon after being loaded onto a blueprint chip for nanoforge production, was stolen by, ironically, a salvaging company turned to piracy.

Designed during the later stages of the early Expansion Epoch of the Domain, the Absolution was conceived as a modern replacement slash supplement for the even-then ageing Invictus pattern hull, intended for deployment where the brick-like battleship was deemed excessive or too costly. As part of the Domain Armada's sweeping modernization drive, the Absolution was fitted with several at-the-time revolutionary features, such as its engines, nowadays not particularly notable but in its time rather overpowered, allowing the Absolution to outspeed almost anything of its weight class. And below, at the time of its first manufacture.

However, during testing, the ship was plagued by a series of unfortunate accidents, friendly fire incidents and more that significantly hindered its chances to pass trials for widespread adoption. One of the primary issues appeared to be the overeagerness of the officers commanding the ship during trials. Reports claim that officers captaining the Absolution, and even the bridge crews under their command, became uncharacteristically overconfident, engaging in aggressive tactics, apparently convinced of their inevitable success. Even normally calm and rational individuals were not immune to this rare condition. And yet, when questioned, they often would not recall many of their actions, even when their crew, under their command, had opened fire on a friendly vessel during cooperative testing operations. This was chalked up to a form of pseudo-combat-stress, brought on by the rather intense testing routine the Absolution was put through.

The aggression phenomenon, meanwhile, was officially attributed to the ship's powerful engines and the bridge's design and camera setup for its holotank emphasising the hull's extensive armament, projecting an illusion of invincibility. Not mentioned publicly were the reported incidences of extreme intrusive thoughts in the bridge crew and officers commanding them, headaches and occasionally nausea for those engaging in maintenance near the bridge and other, more disturbing incidents.
In the end, the Absolution lost the bidding war to the now-famous Onslaught and was adopted only in limited amounts by the Domain Armada, blueprints for the class falling into the hands of the Church of Galactic Redemption after the Collapse, just like the ship it was intended to supplement.

This Absolution variant was discovered inactive within the ship docks of what is now understood to be a well-preserved, private Domain habitat. While Domain standards of insignia mandated Navy ships to be painted according to their associated battlegroup, this ship has been instead matched to the colors of the Domain Navy itself. Data scraped from the vessel's memory indicates it was a "prototype parade-ship"; explaining the unusual paintjob, but not so much the modifications.

The ship has all the hallmarks of a typical Absolution: heavy ballistics integration, uniquely overpowered engines, insulated armor chassis. Notably, however, the ship has been equipped with an unfamiliar engine array; likely prototypical Domain propulsion technology, the engines allow for increased speed and maneuverability in comparison to their standard counterparts, and will reroute power into the weapons arrays when actived for a burn; boosting firerate significantly.

Additionally, the typical inbuilt shield emitters are missing - they have been replaced with an older, external system that is potentially vulnerable to external weapons fire. Instead, the shield emitter is tied to the ship's unusual engines, utilizing a poorly-understood process to "trim" excess power and reroute it directly into the shields; increasing their flux efficiency at higher speeds.

The presence of this ship along with its companion Onslaught, Legion, and Dominator is the subject of some interest. The Absolution-class was never chosen for mass-production for the Domain Navy, having lost its bidding contract to the Onslaught. Its presence aboard the station - as well as the use of its unique "deepstrike" burn drive system in all four recovered ships, nevermind the paintjob and "parade" classification - raises several questions as to its origins and purpose.

The Mule is a rugged and reliable combat-capable freighter which built its reputation on the sparsely-patrolled frontiers of the Domain. Post-collapse, the appeal of the Mule-class has only grown due to the cycles of chaos wracking the Persean Sector, elevating the need for strong armor and powerful weapons to otherwise thrifty traders, scavengers, and prospectors.

The Varanus is exactly what one would expect from looking at its hull silhouette. No gimmicks, no high technology, simply a Monitor combined with a Hammerhead. Inspired by a "design" spewed out by a corrupted nanoforge where residual elements of a Monitor were pasted onto a Hammerhead thanks to a failure to purge data from the last ship produced, the first true Varanus was a prototype produced by one of Kazeron's leading shipyards. Thanks to inherent flaws with the modifications, it didn't pass selection to join the League's navy as a mainline vessel, but it has found a niche of its own, in both Persean League and independent hands. Maintenance costs are high thanks to the aforementioned design flaws and as such it is sometimes looked down upon as a "parade piece" or a "hangar queen", but it inherits some of the bricklike resilience of the Monitor combined with an effective shielding layout, which makes, on paper, a very survivable ship, with Monitor-level resilience in a destroyer-sized package. A brutally efficient statement.

Recall that the Gremlin-class phase vessel was reverse engineered from the firmware of a Nanoforge, a phase rig prototype that was never intended for mass production. The Goblin represents an attempt to salvage the design by reworking it somewhat, while leaving the overall profile of the ship mostly unchanged. The prototype phase coil was replaced with with a later iteration that, while still somewhat unreliable, is far less likely to cause hallucinations and other reported side effects of the phase-wash associated with the Gremlin. The life support systems, similarly, were optimised and somewhat purpose-designed.

A uniquely divisive ship, the St. Bernard, often affectionately referred to as a 'Bernie' by those who captain it and happen to like it, has equally as many admirers as detractors in the Persean Sector. Its design, surprisingly, does not predate the use of shields, but it lacks them anyway, instead using dedicated physical shielding for its cargo and crew, a la several other combat freighters fielded in the Sector. Curiously, the Bernie has the same engine boosting system as the Absolution despite not being manufactured by Orion Shipyards, which lends well to its intended role of rebuffing fighter and bomber raids on logistics while also carrying supplies, aided by its boost system, allowing it to rapidly close in on an ally to defend them. It is rather well armed for a freighter, complete with integrated Devastator Cannon, which its design is contemporaneous to. 

In the post-Collapse reality of the Persean Sector, the Bernie finds itself fulfilling a role not dissimilar to its original purpose, in driving off and destroying pirate vessels as they attack cargo vessels in the fringes of the core worlds and beyond. It is good at this job, so much so that pirate warlord Kanta monetarily rewards those who destroy a St Bernard.
The Bernie is very much a glass cannon design, capable of intense alpha strike damage, but lacking staying power due to a lack of shielding systems, among other things. It offers a risk/reward dilemma to its captains: do they retreat, using its bursts of speed to quickly leave a battlespace, or do they engage and possibly risk having their ship disabled or worse?

A comprehensive refit of the Hound class freighter, the Pitbull is wholly intended as a combat vessel first, and everything else second. Partly inspired by the 'ingenuity' of the Pirates' Mudskipper Mk. II, the Pitbull features a large weapon mounting, and an integration sytsem not unlike that seen in the Onslaught class. Furthermore, to aid in it's fire-support role, the vessel has been equipped with a missile autoforge, based on a modified and hacked forge from a Mora class carrier. Feeding the ship's two built-in sabots, it allows it to have a continual edge in combat, at the cost of versatility.

A technologically advanced frigate with an efficient shield generator and an impressive weapons package that allows it to punch far above its weight. These same characteristics mean its frigate-grade power core struggles to keep up, making careful flux management a priority. 

This variant of the Wolf, fielded by the Hegemony, has had it's weapon systems upgraded, and altered to allow the usage of both ballistic and energy weapons, to allow the ship to fit more easily into the doctrine of the Hegemony's fleets.

Hailing from the age when phase technologies were still unseen in wide-scale deployment, this prototype vessel is one explicitly intended for surveillance first, and combat second. Equipped with an, for the time of it's development, extremely advanced, and compact sensor array. Alongside this, the vessel still retains some of the comforts of it's base hull, having comfortable accommodations intended for long-term, isolated missions.

However, the design ran into several complications in testing, with the sensor array's readings affected by the interference that the ship's phase coil caused when active, meaning that in order to get proper readings, the ship had to risk detection by de-activating it's phase coil, and the phase-field it generated. This, alongside further complications in the vessel's one and only field-test before being shelved, meant that it was never put into full-scale production, or widespread adoption. 

Fabrique Orbitale, having invested much into the project, would quietly put the ship into limited production, advertising it through it's capabilities as a surveillance vessel, and neglecting to mention the effects of a phase-field on crews isolated for extended periods of time. Of course, when sensor suites became capable of detecting phase vessels as standard, what little customers the ship had dwindled even further, making the eccentric vessel a rare oddity in the Persean sector.

A bizarre pre-Collapse design, the Explorator was designed in cooperation between Orion Shipyards and the team responsible for the Termination Sequence drone attack system seen in the Tempest-class frigate. Advertised, even before the fall of the Domain as a mining and exploration vessel for the fringes of human space, the places that had only just about been partially mapped by automated probes. It fulfils its advertised role very well.

Though not particularly well armed, as to be expected from a vessel classified as "civilian", the Explorator is equipped with a fleet of mining drones and accompanying fabrication facilities for which that utilise a variant of the Terminator drone's termination sequence to give the Explorator an unexpected edge in both offense and defense. More than one cocky pirate captain has found themselves in vacuum at the manipulator arms of the modified mining drones of the Explorator.
To say this particular feature was divisive is an understatement, yet through a series of court cases and likely trickery on the behalf of Orion Shipyards, it was approved for production and sale with the mild caveat of only being available for direct sale to the Domain's frontier sectors, such as the Persean Sector. 
The Explorator is not to be underestimated, either by the one captaining it or anyone hoping for an easy kill.

The Ajax-class battlecruiser is a transitory design and it isn't ashamed of it. Inspired by the design of the archaic Retribution class but without certain holdovers, such as the much maligned nuclear pulse propulsion system, the Ajax was one of the final designs by Orion Shipyards that fell into the 'low tech' design school. 'Pocket Onslaught' would be an apt description of its design and intended purpose. What it sacrifices in armour and staying power, it regains in mobility and frontal firepower.

The similarity to the venerable Onslaught extends to more than mere external similarities. Many components that did not need to be designed from scratch are inherited from the Onslaught wholesale, a fact much appreciated by Hegemony quartermasters of the modern day, considering the general state of manufacturing in the Persean Sector. Even if existing Onslaught parts aren't being recycled, only needing one set of design templates for a whole score of replacement parts for not one but two ship designs greatly simplifies logistics.

The catch is that the Ajax only saw limited deployment in the Domain Armada due to the stigma associated with 'low-tech' designs with the exception of the Onslaught, its reputation unfortunately not rubbing off on the Ajax.
This means it is equally as rare in the Hegemony's own fleet, somewhat defeating the purpose of having a battlecruiser design in the first place.

A remnant of the autonomous AI fleets developed by the Tri-Tachyon Corporation. Illegal under Domain (and Hegemony) law, and an abomination to the Church of Galactic Redemption, the First AI War saw these creations purged from the Sector. So the official histories say.

The Mace is an interesting hull design, compared to other mainstays of the Persean League's fleet, such as it is. The existence of the Nanoforge on Kazeron is likely the only reason the Mace exists in the first place, giving the navarchs of Kazeron an excuse to tinker with the ability to theoretically build new whip designs from scratch. The Mace isn't that, although it may seem like it. Developed over a painstaking, years long process after the Collapse, using the basis of a prototype Altair Exotech vessel the name of which nobody could recall, and a recovered 'authentication key', for lack of a better term in order to gain kernel-level access to the chip bearing said blueprint, allowing the Kazeron stratocracy's finest minds to effectively beat the prototype's design into the shape of a new vessel. 

The first Mace surprised everyone involved by not exploding the instant it left the orbital works. Compared to many other ships in the Sector, the vessel is practically a newborn. As such, the Persean League's already divided officer corps, due to its officers being sourced from its constituent worlds albeit with a plurality of Kazeronian origin, and lack of a common culture that results from that, has very little idea of what to do with it. It is very missile heavy armaments wise, fitting of its original, especially well suited to field the Directed Energy Munitions almost emblematic of the Persean League, and would do well as a missile boat to complement the existing doctrine. Unfortunately, it is viewed with much suspicion as a pet project of some bored Kazeronians, an untested design, not having weathered the collapse, and unfortunately this attitude has crept all the way up to what passes for the Persean League's high command, leading to the Mace being relegated to the status of a reserve ship, often falling into the hands of young, inexperienced officers. Either by choice or circumstance because all the other, "better" vessels had been taken already.
The fact the Mace isn't as capable as, say, an Eagle in direct combat further contributes to its odd stigma. Ironically, it would seem it would only be able to prove itself if the League came under serious external threat, at which point there would be bigger concerns than worrying about some new vessel's place in the overall doctrines.

A fearsome ship whose top tier engines provide great speed and maneuverability for a destroyer. This variant of the venerable destroyer is based on a prototype test-bed, the blueprint of which was never supposed to see the light of day. Lacking the energy weaponry and phase skimmer array of it's completed successor, this vessel in-turn has slightly more armor, and an increase in missile firepower. While undoubtedly less capable, it is nonetheless a ship one would be wise not to underestimate.

The Medusa is one of the most respected destroyers in the Sector due to its association with black ops and elite pirates, and the few spacers who have crewed aboard a Medusa can attest to its technological sophistication.

Medusa-class blueprints are few in number and are closely guarded by their owners; pirates have acquired a Medusa-class hull only a handful of times and the results were inevitably drastic, though short-term, threat to local patrols and subsequent reduction in small to medium intrasystem shipping volume. Such events are considered a tremendous nuisance, particularly accounting for increased insurance premiums. Many trade combines will simply call for their fleets to wait for the pirates to run down their new toy's combat readiness so that local authorities can remove the problem once and for all.

Temporarily engages a primary burn on the system travel drive of the ship. Provides a massive speed boost, and boosts the fire rate of all ship weaponry for the duration of the burn. Cannot be toggled once active.

Temporarily engages a burn of the engines and auxilliary thrusters, alongside accelerating ammo feeders. Provides a massive speed boost, and boosts the fire rate of all ship weaponry for the duration of the burn. Cannot be toggled once active.

Deploys a shaped antimatter charge behind the ship. The explosion applied to the ship by these charges has been increased to ludicrious degrees, resulting in the ship incurring varying levels of structural damage with each activation and detenation.
Engages the ship's Lasair Drives and temporarily overloads the engines, propelling the ship great distances with destructive force. Damages the ship and disables weapons on system end.
Activates the heavily modified Deep Strike system of the Absolution (LP), and triggers anti-matter injectors to create a stream of highly destructive fuel in the ship's wake.
Rapidly and drastically increases range and fire rate for the duration of the system.
Ascend into Elysium space on system activation. Temporarily overloads all nearby ships using phase-cloaks or phase-type systems in a radius around the ship.

A design dating to the first explosive expansion of the Domain, this gargantuan mass of armor and all-big-guns was the gauntleted fist that smashed all opposition, spreading hegemony by fear and force over all of spacefaring humanity that was worth conquering.

The steady march of military technology left the hull outdated, however. Its armor design was incompatible with early shield generators, its minimum crew complement staggering, and targeting systems unsophisticated. Modernized replacements were soon developed and the Onslaught-class, among others, was churned out by the great Domain forges. 

An age passed. And, as if by Providence, an expedition sent by the Knights of Ludd discovered an uncorrupted museum archive on a murdered world. A council of inquisitors weighed whether to destroy the Domain-era knowledge, holding a fiery - and secret - debate over the line between sin and virtue, between righteous craft and corrupting technology. An unusually open-minded senior knight-inquisitor examined the contents in detail and persuaded the council to defer the destruction order indefinitely. 

This hull was christened Invictus, a testament to the impossibly heavy armor and vast mass of this absurd cathedral of war. No proper navy would field this monstrosity, but the Church and its Knights can count on a bounty of faithful volunteer-militants to crew the huge munition feeders and crude targeting stations.

The product of a special project by Orion Shipyards, the Hobgoblin class phase destroyer is an early forray into the applications of phase technologies upon military vessels, with the project having partially been the result of a special contract awarded to the corporation by the Domain government, having been narrowly chosen over it's rival, Altair Exotech. Fast, well-armed and surprisingly comfortable for a ship of it's type, the Hobgoblin comes with a hefty maintenance cost relative to it's size, owing to the vessel's ammunition feeders, and specially tuned phase coils. An aggressive statement.

The Reprieve has more than just a passing resemblance to the Invictus-class battleship due to the fact it was designed roughly at the same time as its larger counterpart. Historical details, of course, are scarce, but what little we know indicates the Reprieve ended up complimenting the Invictus in the Domain's earliest fleets, forming "gun-lines" that could annihilate anything that the rest of spacefaring humanity was capable of fielding. Also like the Invictus, it quickly became obsolete, but stuck around longer by virtue of not being as obscenely expensive to crew and supply as its bigger sibling.

A midline destroyer from the golden age of the Domain, the Hammerhead is respected for its staying power in battle as well as its ballistic capabilities. This variant of the ship has been massively overhauled, and upgraded, by the TriTachyon corporation.

A ramshackled, makeshift design produced primarily by pirates, the Konoblin is a frustrating example of 'ingenuity', usually built out of two Gremlin class frigates, in order to create a destroyer sized phase platform. No two Konoblins are the same, and every example seen thus far has been plagued with severe issues stemming from the lack of proper manufacturing capabilities that pirates suffer from. Still, the vessel has proven itself to be useful enough to warrant it's continual usage within various pirate fleets.

An abandoned orbital habitat. A cursory scan indicates that, while it has been cold and dead for tens of cycles at the very least, possibly hundreds, it is in unusually pristine condition. Closer inspection may yield salvage.

This mysterious cruiser was found in long-forgotten deep space, having only been located due to it's poorly-understood connection to it's flagship, the Onslaught Mk.1 recovered from the Orion-Perseus Abyss. While it does not have a recorded identification of its class anywhere within its memory, it most closely resembles an early prototype of a Dominator-class cruiser; though with a number of glaring differences.

While the Dominator-class is renowned for its plentiful ballistic hardpoints in the front of the vessel, this older model is notably different. It's frontal large mounts, instead of being hardpoints, are turreted mounts, allowing the vessel more ease in targeting when compared to the modern Dominator class. Like it's fellow ancients, it too is equipped with extremely robust, albeit ad-hoc, electromechanical automation, allowing it to continue operations from a single unified command despite extreme damage or attrition.

Presumably designed to support the larger Onslaught-class, this primitive Dominator is, just like its modern counterpart, quite capable of punching far above its weight in battle.

This mysterious carrier was found in long-forgotten deep space, having only been located due to its poorly-understood connection to it's flagship, the Onslaught Mk.1 recovered from the Orion-Perseus Abyss. While it does not have a recorded identification of its class anywhere within its memory, it most closely resembles an early prototype of a Legion-class carrier; though with a number of glaring differences.

Like the Onslaught, it is equipped with extremely robust electromechanical automation, allowing it to continue operations from a single unified command despite extreme damage or attrition; though this simple design comes with drawbacks for a complex system that produces fighter-craft. As such, this ancient Legion is quite literal in its description being a "carrier".  Equipped with an ancient model of carrier-type  nanoforge, this aging vessel is incapable of the modern day output seen in it's matured successor, and modern carrier nanoforges overall.

Presumably to account for the increased time needed in combat to affect repairs and reinforcement, this Legion is perhaps the most heavily armored of all its contemporaries - sporting twice the number of armor applique modules, it can soak up tremendous amounts of damage while maintaining strike pressure against the enemies of the Domain.

Ponderous and menacing, the Dominator-class is one of the most widespread system defense cruisers in Domain space. 

While not the most technologically advanced hull, it relies on a plethora of ballistic hardpoints to accomplish its mission, which is more often than not defending orbital installations and vital points of intra-system trade routes. A poor shield emitter which is difficult to manage and thus, rarely engaged, gives way to an almost impregnable interlocking armor belt system making the Dominator safe from most weapons. Even strike craft cannot overcome the hail of projectiles that can be launched to intercept their payloads. This hull proves that tried and true military engineering is difficult to overcome by new ideas and technologies, especially when in the hands of tough, determined crews and experienced officers.

Dependable, durable, and a constant presence in home space around civilized worlds and outposts, the Dominator is perhaps most hated and feared by pirates and law-breaking corporate agents.

A venerable design, the Onslaught-class battleships were first created to serve the Domain Armada long ago, before the development of advanced strike weapons, modern energy weapons, and shield systems. 

When first launched from orbital dock, their firepower and burst-speed surely intimidated entire systems. Some even say that they were built to combat non-humans in a long forgotten war. Much later, Orion Shipyards engineers made modifications to the blueprints to include a shield system, upgraded the hyperdrive, and reduced the required crew complement through automation and iterative engineering. Even though more advanced blueprints are available, the Onslaught remains the easiest to manufacture due to the brutal simplicity of its systems. 

A ship designed without shields in mind, built to be able to withstand a heavy barrage of enemy fire and strike back while protecting its crew is much loved by its officers and crew. And strike back it can; the Onslaught's unmatched ballistic potential can devastate entire fleets in minutes, its only drawback a logistical dependency on ammunition. 

Onslaught crews are proud to serve in the class which forms the backbone of the Hegemony Navy.

Classified as a battlecarrier, the Legion mounts an impressive array of heavy weapons, hangar-space, and command-control sufficient to field four fighter wings. Later models were upgraded with nanoforges keyed to replacement of fightercraft, significantly increasing tooth-to-tail ratio on distant deployments.

After the legendary success of the Onslaught design it became clear that rebellious systems without ultra-heavy industry were able to develop carrier-based strike-craft capable of countering the 'Old Man' of the Armada. Alongside new weapons - nimble anti-fighter missiles and rapid-tracking point defense cannon - the Strategic Council decided to deploy a carrier worthy of service alongside the Onslaught. Thus the Legion was designed to provide a platform for interceptors and strike-craft while standing on the line of battle. 

Proponents of the 'Cruiser School' criticized the Legion for insufficient specialization, maintaining that similar fighter volume can be fielded at less cost and greater flexibility if combat roles are separated into distinct ship hulls. These economic arguments do pale in the face of an incoming Legion engaging its burn drive to deliver crushing firepower at the key point of battle.

After the legendary success of the Onslaught design it became clear that rebellious systems without ultra-heavy industry were able to develop carrier-based strike-craft capable of countering the 'Old Man' of the Armada. Alongside new weapons - nimble anti-fighter missiles and rapid-tracking point defense cannon - the Strategic Council decided to deploy a carrier worthy of service alongside the Onslaught. Thus the Legion was designed to provide a platform for interceptors and strike-craft while standing on the line of battle. 

Proponents of the 'Cruiser School' criticized the Legion for insufficient specialization, maintaining that similar fighter volume can be fielded at less cost and greater flexibility if combat roles are separated into distinct ship hulls. These economic arguments do pale in the face of an incoming Legion engaging its burn drive to deliver crushing firepower at the key point of battle.

Built to the specifications of the 14th Domain Battlegroup which founded the Hegemony, this vessel is a prime example of the Domain Navy's 'decisive battle' doctrine, particularly exhibited by a series of radical structural modifications performed using pre-Collapse industrial technology. A venerable design, the Onslaught-class battleships were first created to serve the Domain Armada long ago, before the development of advanced strike weapons, modern energy weapons, and shield systems. 

When first launched from orbital dock, their firepower and burst-speed surely intimidated entire systems. Some even say that they were built to combat non-humans in a long forgotten war. Much later, Orion Shipyards engineers made modifications to the blueprints to include a shield system, upgraded the hyperdrive, and reduced the required crew complement through automation and iterative engineering. Even though more advanced blueprints are available, the Onslaught remains the easiest to manufacture due to the brutal simplicity of its systems. 

A ship designed without shields in mind, built to be able to withstand a heavy barrage of enemy fire and strike back while protecting its crew is much loved by its officers and crew. And strike back it can; the Onslaught's unmatched ballistic potential can devastate entire fleets in minutes, its only drawback a logistical dependency on ammunition. 

Onslaught crews are proud to serve in the class which forms the backbone of the Hegemony Navy.

Built to the specifications of the 14th Domain Battlegroup which founded the Hegemony, this vessel is a prime example of the Domain Navy's 'decisive battle' doctrine, particularly exhibited by a series of radical structural modifications performed using pre-Collapse industrial technology. Ponderous and menacing, the Dominator-class is one of the most widespread system defense cruisers in Hegemony space. 

While not the most technologically advanced hull, it relies on a plethora of ballistic hardpoints to accomplish its mission, which is more often than not defending orbital installations and vital points of intra-system trade routes. A poor shield emitter which is difficult to manage and thus, rarely engaged, gives way to an almost impregnable interlocking armor belt system making the Dominator safe from most weapons. Even strike craft cannot overcome the hail of projectiles that can be launched to intercept their payloads. This hull proves that tried and true military engineering is difficult to overcome by new ideas and technologies, especially when in the hands of tough, determined crews and experienced officers.

Dependable, durable, and a constant presence in home space around civilized worlds and outposts, the Dominator is perhaps most hated and feared by pirates and law-breaking corporate agents.

Built to the specifications of the 14th Domain Battlegroup which founded the Hegemony, this vessel is a prime example of the Domain Navy's 'decisive battle' doctrine, particularly exhibited by a series of radical structural modifications performed using pre-Collapse industrial technology. It is not hard to see why: A strong overall profile, with a robust engine, the Eagle's deadly weapons package is a threat to all enemies.

The Eagle can deliver a strong tactical punch to enemy formations. Its numerous turret and hardpoint emplacements make it very dangerous to smaller foes. Decent armor and a strong shield emitter let it hold space while outnumbered, or even when faced with the rare larger ship. 

These strengths are somewhat countered by strike craft - an Eagle captain must always watch their scopes for an approaching strike squadron, since their ship will be easily crippled by multiple hits from modern strike weapons. 

The embodiment of the sleek and powerful space cruiser from the time of the Domain, the Eagle-class ships are a beautiful reminder of the technological and aesthetic achievements of humanity's past.

Often called the Eagle cruiser's little brother, the Falcon-class cruiser sacrifices armor for speed, neatly filling the light cruiser role in military fleets throughout the Sector. 

The light designation does not indicate a significant reduction in firepower, however, making the Falcon a valuable tactical asset to any fleet. The ship is easily able to fill a wide variety of roles, from close support to assault, given the proper configuration. 

The Falcon's top notch engines give it the ability to quickly disengage from battle should its defenses be pressed to a critical point.

Swift and elegant, Falcon-class cruisers are often found as lead elements in larger fleet formations, or deployed to reinforce anti-pirate convoys.

The Enforcer-class ships commonly serve in system or convoy defense roles. The design features good armor and multiple ballistic hardpoints, while shield performance is somewhat underwhelming. 

The blueprints of the ship call for many components similar to those found in the Onslaught-class battleships, suggesting that the designs were created during a similar period of military expansion in the Domain. The Enforcer-class features similar no-nonsense weapon system design choices, tough bulkheads, and is well regarded by its crews.

Tough to beat in a destroyer to destroyer fight, the Enforcer rarely takes part in larger battles due to the common view that its low speed makes it a liability. Nonetheless, Hegemony order of battle doctrines mandate an attached Enforcer squadron as a screen for Onslaught-class battleships. The logistical ease with which shared components can be used by both ship types is exactly the type of detail that excites Hegemony logistics bureaucrats.
An ancient, resilient design of drone fighter from a bygone era.

A high tech destroyer in the same family of the famous Apogee class, the Culmination is the result of a program which desired to bring similar exploratory capabilities, in a smaller form factor. A somewhat odd thing, this destroyer is rarely seen in the modern persean sector, thanks to only having been produced in limited amounts prior to the collapse. Before, of course, it's blueprint was recovered during an expedition outside the coreworlds.

The result of observations following the initial failure yet eventual success of the Odyssey-class battlecruiser, the Iliad was intended to be a more coherent successor to the allegedly AI designed vessel. Based upon the often overlooked Conquest-class in order to save time in the design phase, the Iliad's creation process was, at first, rather smooth. Unfortunately, the project was soon plagued by both budget constraints and increased demands, simultaneously from higher departments as well as potential customers. This resulted in several rushed aspects and design concessions being forced into the vessel to appease timeline constraints, conflicting cutting-edge systems shoved haphazardly into the ungainly spheroid hull. The result was, begrudgingly, well-received and moderately successful, but the issues plaguing it prevented it from reaching a wider market than those investors suffering from sunk-cost fallacy, with the occasional exception of a particularly delusional Odyssey-class captain.

A midline destroyer from the golden age of the Domain, the Hammerhead is respected for its staying power in battle as well as its ballistic capabilities. Fit with extreme modifications by it's Luddic Path crew, this vessel has been turned into a 'holy' weapon of war.

The Champion-class heavy cruiser is a versatile warship featuring a range of powerful energy weapons; the crowning element is a heavy energy turret mounting, rare among midline ships. This offensive array is backed by a robust energy grid capable of supercharging the energy weapon loadout, increasing damage output to devastating levels. A heavy missile hardpoint complements the loadout by enabling the Champion to unleash a crippling strike without taxing flux levels. The Champion is a solid and capable contender, able to face capital ships on the battle-line. This variant has been heavily modified, with a highly illegal autonomous conversion having been performed.

A relatively recent design, the Champion is a product of the historically recent "Cruiser School" naval revolution that never saw active service in the pre-collapse Domain Armada. Although prototypes were constructed and forge-ready specifications distributed to several battlegroups, the Champion was never cleared for active deployment due to an ongoing lawsuit between Altair Exotech and Orion Shipyards. Each megacorp accused the other of industrial espionage and inappropriately influencing the Armada officers overseeing the procurement process. The truth was more complex, inflaming longstanding rivalries in the officer corps as the investigatory committee called witness after witness. The Collapse prevented any sort of conclusive ruling from reaching the Persean Sector however, and now the entire matter is considered irrelevant. With the discovery of Champion plans on a Domain armaments courier, the warship was quickly put into service by the fleet of the Persean League, among others.

The idea of such a vessel being converted to have phase capabilities would be anathema to most engineers within the sector, and appaling to any proud Hegemony officer, or faithful follower of Ludd. And yet, here it is.

While not usually the most technologically advanced hull, it relies on a plethora of ballistic hardpoints to accomplish its mission, which is more often than not defending orbital installations and vital points of intra-system trade routes. It's poor shield emitter has been entirely replaced by a phase coil system, it's internals having been entirely and professionally overhauled, something out of scope even within the wealth that operating in a legal gray area can pose. Evidence within the ship's logs, though limited, alludes to Tri-Tachyon influence within the conversion process of this vessel.

A Tri-Tachyon special project created with the explicit purpose of wowing potential investors and creating confidence in it's drone-ship projects, the Elucidation class heavy cruiser incorporates several highly advanced technologies in a relatively small, and mobile package. Given the lack of a human crew and thus the necessary concessions for one, it gave Tri-Tachyon's engineers ample space to pack in a weapon suite that could be considered absurd for a cruiser-scale vessel, alongside an energy-bolt-coherence system to further facilitate it's lethality in combat.

Thought to have only been produced in the single digits prior to the onset of the first AI war, these examples were thought confiscated or destroyed in the aftermath of the conflict, but reports of vessels matching it's descriptions do yet exist, shared amongst the odd paranoid spacer, or word-of-mouth legend, and any spacer would be wise to hope that that's what they are. Just legends.
Temporarily overcharges both the engine and weaponry systems of the ship.

What is there to be said about the Thgualsno? It is exactly what it looks like to even the most casual observer: an Onslaught class battleship, but wrong in every way. Its engines are mounted where the Thermal Pulse Cannons would be positioned on a standard Onslaught. Its many, many missile mounts are, likewise, where the engines should be on an Onslaught. 

There are many contradictory tales of how this ship came to be, but there are two that stand out as the most repeated and plausible. The first is that a particularly ambitious pirate warlord invested vast amounts of time and credits into cracking the encryption, or just scraping the data of, an Onslaught blueprint for mass production via a stolen nanoforge. The end result was supposedly the first Thgualsno, the sight of which driving the warlord over the edge and causing him to space himself, his warband breaking up after his death. The other is that the first Thgualsno was found by pirates scouring the outer reaches of the Sector. In a dead system that was scoured by the First AI War, a malfunctioning nanoforge, yet still barely functioning, spat out the design once fed a small amount of metal, enough to finalise it. Data corruption due to exposure to hard radiation over a period of years somehow produced a design that human eyes could comprehend, if barely. The resulting glitched Onslaught blueprint was copied and sold to both black and open market channels, explaining how non-pirate operated versions of this ship even exist in the first place.

Still, it is nonetheless a phase ship of the low-tech variety, and as such, is subject to all of the misgivings spacer crews have come to associate with these type of vessels, even if it is more comfortable than it's gremlin sibling.

Firstly intended to replace the Hathoda-class orbital siege-capable heavy ballistic weapons platform, then considered a capital-class warship in its own right before the 4th Domain Armada Revised Schema reclassification order, the Kardakes was first deployed to battle conditions during the retaking of the Eridani Insurrection's gains in previous cycles. The Kardakes-class heavy cruiser proved itself a fine addition to the Domain's naval arsenal as it's heavy armor allowed it to sustain damage that would have surely crippled any other class, save the aging Hathoda. Following the Eridani Insurrection and subsequent campaigns, the Kardakes-class would then go on to lay the doctrinal framework for it's eventual replacement, the Dominator-class heavy cruiser.

Born out of a Domain contract-race between several smaller design companies, the Erebid was intended to fill out a niche doctrine among the lower officers of the Domain Armada, that of a hit-and-run ship for fast attack, to be newly classed as an "assault craft". 

In many ways the "bigger brother" of the aging Vanguard-class heavy frigate, the Erebid employs the same resonant-field-dampening technology to aid in it's role, allowing it's already impressive armor to sustain even further damage while active to facilitate retreat and relocation on the battlefield.

"Armada leadership, most of whom escaped direct prosecution via the 'Grey Wave' which saw nearly four hundred senior officers resign following the megadeath incident at Hipparcos, and the subsequent containment campaign, called for an emergency hearing regarding fabrication technology security and safety, the Interstellar Quality and Design Assurance Reforms. 

The results of the Interstellar Quality and Design Assurance Reforms - a series of acts passed over an energetic dozen cycles by the representative body of the Human Domain and only so-called by later historians - which build the legal basis for sweeping enforcement of fabrication rights management (henceforth the QDAR reforms), were mandatory security protocols to be implemented in every Universal Access Chip following the passing of the act. Those that failed to comply were fined heavily, and in some cases, had their assets seized, with control of the company either falling to the Domain itself. Or, more often, having it's assets divided and sold to other corporations following the implementation of these security protocols.

While few live to tell of what happened in those tense months that comprised the Hipparcos Containment, it has nonetheless left a scar on the Domain at large. One that may never truly heal."

A standout of Orion Shipyards design in the post-'Emerald Age' exodus, this frontier-rated utility platform featured a spinal-mount microwave emitter modulated for orbit-to-orbit operations. Alongside this, the platform is also capable of orbit-to-surface energy transferral, though this results in the emitter placing far more strain on the vessel's reactor, varying on the distance. Furthermore, this emitter cannot be used on worlds that have habitable atmospheres. Such caveats ensured that the Fulgurite saw both limited adoption in more civilized spaces, and expectedly, wide-spread adoption within frontier sectors, where such concerns were less prevalent.
A heavily damaged invictus.

An enormous composite-beam laser system with near-omnidirectional coverage integrated into the forward hull of the Galaxy-class battlecruiser. Equally capable of engaging enemy ships and acting as a high-powered point defense system.

The pride of Altair Exotech R&D's Division 72, the High-Energy Laser Interception and Offense System was conceived as a radical new breed of point defense system for the in-development Galaxy-class battlecruiser. With a proprietary multitargeting emitter "strip" and a lasing medium directly pumped by the vessel's main reactor, the initial design brief promised a rare combination of wide-area coverage, pinpoint accuracy, and respectable firepower.

The realities of engineering, however, ultimately set in, and while the production-model HELIOS Array was not the impenetrable aegis against missiles and strikecraft it was meant to be, it is still a marvel of energy weapon technology, with the power output to threaten full-size warships and the efficiency and precision to fire on targets in nearly any direction as fast as gunnery crews can lock on.

But with the Collapse of gates come the collapse of Eridani Terraforming initiative, leaving the planet in a major financial void. Tri Tachyon corporation stepped in and stabilized the situation for a while, but weren?t able to prevent revolt which swept through the Insulinde system. A new antidomain movement claimed power and cut off all external trade, complicating the situation even more. 
In the resulting siege of the system, Deora was bombarded into stone age, finally destroying the barely holding ecosystem. Remaining rebel elements retreated in rural regions where they survive to this day.

Revachol once in the past was capital of Suzerainty of Revachol under the forgotten Domain's noble family, now an unstable and polluted world, famous for its low taxes and unlimited commerce. 

After the Collapse planet fell into barely contained chaos. Local nobles used more and more crude methods of maintaining power, until internal pressure toppled over and the planet became the center of antidomain revolution, which later spread to the whole system. But the new regime didn?t hold long, reactionary movements formed and when Tri-Tachion moved to claim the planet they were forced to cut the deal with reactionaries, allowing the planet to maintain its independence and reclaim mining station under special provisions.

Revachol's mining station is major supplier of resources in the system. Mining rich outer asteroid belts, station always was fuel under all major industry in the system, and it maintains this status to this day.

Compared to the chaos on other major population centers of the star system, Revachol's mining station, was always small enough to make any power struggles too costly, so they just sweared their loyalty to any dominant power in the system, while struggling to establish any sort of supply routes to keep people fed and healthy and station?s systems from collapsing.

While plainly sharing design aspects and proprietary technology, the corporation vehemently denied any an all involvement with the project when it became public knowledge in an unusual incident.

What has been gleamed from fragmentary Domain history is that the Meridian was apparently commissioned in anticipation of a wave of civil unrest or insurrection. From where this expected insurrection was expected to arise is unknown, but many analysts have pointed out that the Meridian itself appears to be a ship custom-made to counter standard battlegroup task forces.

An odd example of domain era starship design by Altair Exotech, the Culmination class was a foray into experimental technologies, and the combat exploration line that began with the famous Apogee class exploration cruiser. Most prominent among those experimental technologies having been it's HELIOS array, an integrated particle beam weapon directly built into the ship.

While the vessel saw somewhat limited military adoption, it's versatile suite of science facilities, spacious and near-luxurious crew quarters, and high resolution sensor package saw it gain high praise, and popularity amongst independent explorers, and surveyors on the frontiers of Domain space.

Though nominally designated as a "trade ship", the large weapon mounts and aggressive layout of the ship makes itself obvious to even the most oblivious bureaucrat that the Decorum is a vessel primarily meant for raiding. 

Infamy plagued the ship; even before it began production, its blueprints were stolen by an equally shady corporation, who then attempted to pawn it off to Domain Procurement. The following legal battle resulted in the Decorum's blueprints being leaked to the public, creating an instant favorite among pirates and insurrectionists for its speed and frontal power.

These strengths are somewhat countered by strike craft - an Eagle captain must always watch their scopes for an approaching strike squadron, since their ship will be easily crippled by multiple hits from modern strike weapons. 

The embodiment of the sleek and powerful space cruiser from the time of the Domain, the Eagle-class ships are a beautiful reminder of the technological and aesthetic achievements of humanity's past.

The voluminous but ungainly hull of the Mbaye-Gogol 430 "Nebula" does little to enhance the romance of interstellar travel but it does ensure a respectable passenger and cargo capacity for a ship of its class. Indeed, the Nebula has slowly come to dominate mid-tier passenger service since the muted reception of its first line of production. This variant has been modified into a cheap, ungainly weapons platform by Pirates.

The Nebula is equipped with a forward-facing shield to enhance the safety of passengers and extend the hull plating's maintenance schedule. And the Sector being what it is, several ballistic turrets and anti-missile all-band flare launchers have been mounted at fortuitous locations to assure paying passengers that their well-being is a top priority of the operator.

The go-to choice for medium cargo hauling in the Sector, the Buffalo-class freighter exemplifies the "Load-n-Pray" principle prevalent in Sector shipping. This variant has been modified by the Luddic Path into a poor weapon of "holy" war.

Sporting just a single small weapon emplacement, the hull of the ship is no more than a large engine with a tiny crew quarters section and cargo grapplers. A captain taking this ship out without a convoy rarely gets to make the same mistake twice. Incapable of anything resembling a combat maneuver, the lateral thrusters on Buffalo-class ships are designed to merely enable it to dock when (and if) it reaches its destination.

The ship engines are the greatest contributor to hull cost, which, while low, is still within the norms for a medium freighter. The greatest contributing factor to its ubiquity is the fact that the blueprint for this ship is usually hardcoded into every orbital shipyard's blueprint database.

Designed during a transitory phase of ship design, the Bullshark is designed to enter the battlespace as quickly as possible, soften up the enemy with its respectable array of weaponry, then unleash its fighters to deliver the heavy blow.

Its mixed weaponry betrays a transitory origin. Designed right before the renaissance of the "Cruiser School" in ship design, the Bullshark was quickly eclipsed by its leaner, faster cousins. However, the ship did find a respectable niche in the role of a command carrier, able to act as the central nexus of a carrier group while still keeping pace with its smaller escorts.
An experimental battleship that was slated to be produced by the Persean League, but ultimately cancelled.
